subject: Duplicate request IDs causing double-counting — reconciliation plan
messages:
From: Aileen Park <aileen@quantaai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Quanta AI Billing <billing@quantaai.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected double charges on last invoice — possible duplicate request IDs

Hi Logan,

We're seeing a ~2x spike in our Aug invoice line item for token usage tied to the embeddings endpoint. The timing lines up with a batch import run on Aug 31, but our internal logs show the job submitted identical request_ids for a subset of retries (we have idempotency enabled). Can you confirm whether Redwood's metering deduplicates on request_id or per-call?

Attached is a small sample from our side (first 150 rows) showing request_id, timestamp, and payload hash. We suspect the following sequence:
- Job retries re-used the same request_id in two processes due to a race during orchestration.
- Redwood counted both attempts as separate tokens rather than deduplicating.

We flagged this with our finance team and they put the invoice on hold pending your reconciliation. If it's on us, we'll cover. If it's on Redwood metering, we need a quick path to a pro-rata credit for the duplicated tokens and a corrected invoice for our AP team.

Can you escalate to billing ops and let us know the expected timeline? We're trying to close this month-end.

Thanks,
Aileen Park
Head of Data Platform, Quanta AI
Aileen | @aileen-park

Attachment(s): sample_requestids_aug31.csv (csv)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Park <aileen@quantaai.com>
Cc: Quanta AI Billing <billing@quantaai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected double charges on last invoice — possible duplicate request IDs

Hi Aileen — thanks for the sample and flag.

Short answer: Redwood's metering tries to deduplicate at the request_id level for hosted API calls, but there are a few cases (concurrent retries hitting different frontends before request_id propagation completes) that can result in double-counting. I cc'd Vanessa from Billing Ops and Marcus from Platform so we can triage.

Next steps I'll take now:
1) Vanessa: can you pull the token-level usage export for Quanta AI for Aug 31 — preferably the raw log with request_id and token counts per call?
2) Marcus: can you check whether any frontends reported failing idempotency lookup for the Quanta account in that 22:00–23:30 UTC window?
3) Aileen: if you can send the 1k-row sample (or your full job run id), that'll speed verification.

I know you mentioned AP hold. We'll aim to get back with a reconciliation plan within 48 hours. If it's on our side, we will propose a pro-rata credit and corrected invoice ASAP.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Book time: https://cal.com/logan/15

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aileen Park <aileen@quantaai.com>, Quanta AI Billing <billing@quantaai.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected double charges on last invoice — possible duplicate request IDs

Logan / Marcus / Aileen — quick update from Billing Ops after pulling the raw usage export and cross-checking against request traces. Summary:

- We retrieved the token-level export for Quanta AI for 2026-08-31 21:45–23:45 UTC (attached). The export includes fields: timestamp, request_id, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, total_tokens, frontend_id.
- We found ~14,322 tokens that appear duplicated across two distinct call records that share the same request_id but different frontend_id and distinct backend_trace_id. The pattern matches a replay: two incoming requests with same request_id reached different frontends before the idempotency cache was updated.
- For the affected request_ids, the two records show identical prompt_hash and near-identical token counts (one had +1 token in completion due to a trailing newline).

Proposed remediation:
1) We will issue a pro-rata credit for the duplicated tokens (amount shown in this CSV). Total preliminary credit: $1,032.45.
2) We'll adjust the August invoice and provide a corrected PDF within 3 business days so your AP team can resume payment.
3) Platform will schedule a short config patch to tighten idempotency propagation across frontends; this is low-risk and should be deployed in the Sept maintenance window.

Attachments: usage_export_20260904.csv (csv), support_trace_log.txt (txt)

Aileen — please confirm you accept this plan and whether the credit should be applied against the Aug invoice or carried forward as account credit. If you accept, we'll start the invoice amendment and cc your AP contact on the revised billing doc.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Aileen Park <aileen@quantaai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Quanta AI Billing <billing@quantaai.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected double charges on last invoice — possible duplicate request IDs

Hi Vanessa / Logan — thanks for the quick investigation and the clear plan. Quanta accepts the proposed remediation: please apply the $1,032.45 credit against the Aug invoice and send the corrected invoice to billing@quantaai.com.

For our records we'll need:
- A short note in the invoice metadata saying "pro-rata credit applied for duplicated metering (request_id replay)" plus the list of affected request_ids (a separate attachment is fine).
- Expected date the corrected invoice will be published (you mentioned up to 3 business days).

Once we have the corrected PDF we'll release the hold and route payment. Appreciate you looping Marcus on the propagation fix — please keep us posted if you need a test window from our side.

Best,
Aileen
